The plan's recommended H1 — 'Aglyn AI: for agencies and multi-brand teams, an AI website builder that drafts what you describe' — is 96 characters and the skeleton's H1 is 72px Black in a 600px column, so the hero heading below is the short form and the hero body carries the head term and the audience. disclosure.body: Aglyn AI is a release-flagged feature, currently being rolled out — the doors described on this page do not all appear in every workspace yet. Aglyn Assist, the assistant that answers questions about the product, is available today.
disclosure.notes: Generative building is gated on `release_ai_generative`, which is OFF in production: every generative route answers 404, so a page that reads as though Aglyn AI is available today would be a misrepresentation on the live site. The wording is the one `apps/docs/docs/ai/overview.md` has carried all along, so the two surfaces agree. It is a DISCRETE element on purpose: when the flag flips, this band is deleted and the page is correct, rather than the page being rewritten sentence by sentence — the same way the `:::caution Rolling out` admonitions come out of the docs. The second sentence is the honest split: `release_assist` gates the assistant that answers questions and has been on since 2026-08-23, and `libs/plugins/ai/src/lib/server/ai-assist.ts` carries no release flag at all, while `release_ai_generative` gates every build job (`ai-jobs-gate.ts`, `ai-jobs-route.ts`, `assist-chat.ts`). A page that blurs the two undersells what works or oversells what does not. ⛔ `apply-page-copy.js` pours `sections` and nothing else, so this band is NOT poured — it is placed by hand in the same pass, and deleted by hand at the flip.

sections.eyebrow: AGLYN AI · DESCRIBE IT, EDIT IT
sections.heading: Describe it. Get a draft. Edit anything.
body: Aglyn AI is an AI website builder inside the console you already run. Describe a page, a whole small site, a form, a reusable component, an email or a campaign, and it builds a draft from your own theme, layout and components — for you to edit, and for you to publish.

image.describe: AI jobs panel mockup, 920×580, floating card with the hero shadow. Header 'AI jobs' with a close glyph and a job chip 'Needs review'. The job at the top reads 'Describe a page' with the brief beneath it in quotes: 'A services page for a two-person landscaping company — what we do, before-and-after photos, and a quote request form.' Below it the PLAN, in three labeled groups. 'Reuse' lists three rows with a recycle glyph: Layout · Site header & footer; Component · Service card; Form · Quote request. 'Create' lists two rows with a plus glyph: Section · Before and after, because the site has no gallery component; Dataset · Services, proposed from the six services in the brief. 'Screens' lists one row: /services · Site header & footer · 'Landscaping services in Ashford'. Bottom bar: an estimate chip reading 'Estimated · 1,850 credits', a text button 'Cancel' and a primary button 'Confirm plan'. Right of the panel, a second, smaller card labeled 'Draft · not published' showing a page thumbnail with an 'Open draft' link and a small amber row reading '1 gap to fill: [phone number]'.

sections.notes: Two columns: 600px text column left (80px left inset, no right padding), mockup right, bleeding off the right edge — the deliberate container-overflow exception the skeleton records. Eyebrow is the 28×2px magenta rule plus the uppercase tracked label. Heading is Display/XL 72px Black and fits three short sentences on two lines at that size. ⛔ The mockup is the page's one chance to show the draft-first rule without prose, so it must show a PLAN awaiting confirmation and a DRAFT that is not published — never a published page, never a live URL, never a Send button. The credits figure is illustrative and is flagged in `claimsToVerify`; it carries no dollar amount, and no plan tier or price may appear anywhere in this shot. The '1 gap to fill' row is building rule 14 (`apps/docs/docs/ai/how-aglyn-ai-builds.md`), which marks a missing fact in square brackets rather than inventing it.

sections.heading: Most AI builders hand you a finished website and dare you to change it. Aglyn AI hands you a draft — made from your own components, your layout and your theme — and every part of it opens in the editor you already use.
sections.notes: Single full-bleed 34px Bold pull-quote at text/muted (#757575), 80px side padding, 64px vertical, left-aligned. The phrase 'a draft' is emphasized in text/primary (#212121) — the rest stays muted, as on the Console page where 'one place' carries the emphasis. The first clause is a claim about the shape of the category, not about a named competitor, so it is outside `check:external-facts` and outside the comparison rule; nothing here concedes or asserts anything about another vendor. Keep it that way — a named product in this slot becomes an `/alternatives/*` row with a verification burden.

sections.heading: A draft for most of what you make.

items.title: Pages, and whole small sites
items.body: Describe a page and it builds a screen in your layout. Describe a business and it plans a small site — the pages, their addresses, a shared layout and a contact form — before it builds anything.

items.title: Layouts, templates, components
items.body: A header, navigation and footer as one layout. A page template for pages that differ only by content. A block that repeats built once as a reusable component.

items.title: Forms that are ready to collect
items.body: Describe a form and it arrives on the Forms page with its fields, the answers it requires, a marketing consent box when it asks for an email address, and where each submission goes.

items.title: Emails, campaigns and follow-ups
items.body: A draft email built from the email blocks, with three subject lines to choose between — or that design plus the draft campaign that would send it. In the CRM, a summary of where a record stands and a one-to-one email drafted into the composer.

items.title: Copy, themes, listings and products
items.body: Rewrite any text on the canvas, or write it from nothing. Describe a theme change and get a proposal in the theme editor's own controls. Have a page or product's search listing written, and a product's copy and catalog ideas proposed.

items.title: Your figures, and what to try next
items.body: Plain-words answers about your own numbers, with every figure traced to the row it came from. Where your plan includes A/B testing, two to four variants of the copy under test — and a result read back in words that names a winner only when the numbers support one.

sections.notes: Centered eyebrow and heading, 3-column card grid, 2 rows, 410px cards with the 44px icon tile top-left. The grid is SIX cards and cannot grow — `apply-page-copy.js` pins this section at 14 slots for every product page — so a new door is folded into an existing card rather than given its own, which is why cards 4, 5 and 6 each carry more than one. ⛔ Card 6 is the only claim on this page that needs more than the AI add-on: A/B testing is an entitlement of its own, so the clause 'Where your plan includes A/B testing' is load-bearing and must not be trimmed for rhythm. ⛔ These six are the released doors and no more. Drafting an automation from a description is NOT among them — `apps/docs/docs/ai/automations-with-ai.md#draft` says the door is shut on every plan because a multi-step description can come back as a one-step draft. Explaining an automation you already have, and answering why a run failed, ARE released, and they sit in the deep-dive rather than here so that no card reads as 'AI builds your automations'. The heading deliberately says 'most of what you make' rather than a count: `project_product_roster_is_ten_no_counters` bans a counter in copy, and a list of doors goes stale on every release.

sections.heading: It builds. You publish.
body: Every generation writes a draft, or a new unpublished version of something you already have. It never flips a published version, never registers an address on your live site, never changes your navigation and never sends anything. Publishing stays yours, through the buttons you already use.

items.title: A plan before any work
items.body: Each build job first proposes what it will reuse, what it will create and why, and what each screen will hold. Nothing is generated until you confirm it.

items.title: Built from what you already have
items.body: Your layout, your components, your forms, your theme's colors and spacing — checked against the building rules before you see it, and asked again when an answer breaks one.

items.title: It proposes; you decide
items.body: A job you don't like costs the credits it spent and a draft you delete. A proposal fills in the fields you would have typed — it never starts a test or moves a visitor. It can also simply read what you have: what a saved automation does, or why a run failed.

image.describe: Besigner canvas mockup, 768×580, showing a generated page open as a draft. Top bar carries the screen name 'Services', a grey status pill reading 'Draft · never published', and a primary 'Publish' button that is the only way it goes live. Left rail shows the layer tree with a highlighted 'Service card' component instance repeated three times — one component, three instances, not three copies. Right rail shows the Attributes panel with theme tokens selected rather than hex values ('Primary', 'Spacing 4'). Across the canvas, a services section with three cards and a quote form block labeled 'Quote request · placed by reference'. Bottom-left, a small toast: 'Draft created. Nothing on your live site has changed.'

sections.notes: Combined deep-dive + canvas/visual section — the page's one big visual moment. Two columns: 440px text column left, 768px mockup right, on the tinted band. The three items are checkmark-bulleted rows, not cards. This section carries the single most load-bearing true claim on the page, so its body is close to verbatim from `apps/docs/docs/ai/overview.md#drafts-only` and building rule 13 — the four nevers are the ones the product actually enforces, and no one of them may be softened or dropped for rhythm. Item three does three jobs. 'Costs the credits it spent and a draft you delete' is the abandon case. 'A proposal fills in the fields you would have typed — it never starts a test or moves a visitor' is the A/B door stated as its code states it: the variants widget writes into the experiment editor's own fields, unsaved, and the dialog's Save is the only write (`libs/plugins/marketing/src/lib/components/experiment-zones.tsx`). And 'simply read what you have' is exactly what Explain it and Why did this fail? do, neither of which drafts nor runs anything.

sections.heading: From one sentence to something you can edit.

items.title: Describe it
items.body: Open the page that lists what you want built — Screens, Layouts, Templates, Forms or Components — and choose Describe it beside its create button.

items.title: Read the plan
items.body: The job answers with a plan: what it will reuse, what it will create and why, and the screens it will build. Confirm it to build, or cancel and pay nothing more.

items.title: Edit, then publish
items.body: The draft opens in the editor you already use. Change anything, fill the gaps it marked in square brackets, and publish when you are ready.

sections.notes: LEFT-aligned eyebrow and heading, three equal columns each topped by a 3px rule, then the 2-digit step numeral, title and body. `meta` here is the step numeral and IS display copy — the opposite of the early-access band below, where `meta: 'stat'` is the extractor's type tag. AGL-1233 published the literal word 'stat' on eight pages by flattening the two the same way; the applier now flattens them differently and `verify-applier.mjs` asserts the values rather than the count.

sections.notes: TEN link-cards on a pale grey band, centered eyebrow, heading and subheading. The ten are the roster (`project_product_roster_is_ten_no_counters`); Aglyn AI is not one of them, so there is no self-link to omit and no Datasets card — /product/datasets sits outside the roster, which is why its own Explore grid carries these same ten. Every title and blurb is verbatim from `copy-datasets.json` so the grids stay identical across pages; changing one here silently forks it. The heading follows the live detail pages' '<Product> works with the rest of Aglyn.' and the subheading is the one seven of them share. ⛔ The grid must be grown from seven cards to ten BEFORE pouring — `apply-page-copy.js` takes this section's slot count from `explore.items` and refuses a canvas whose grid holds a different number — and each card's `screenId` re-pointed from the screens table at apply time, never transcribed from a dry run.

sections.heading: Aglyn AI is an add-on on every paid plan.
body: Bought once for the workspace — not per seat and not per site — it adds a band of AI credits to the band your plan already includes, and every member with the permission can use it on every site. A door built on a plan feature needs that feature too: AI A/B variants need A/B testing on your plan as well as the add-on. Free workspaces get a small monthly allowance instead, and stop there rather than billing you.

items.body: credit pool for the whole workspace
pages published without you
tries, then a job stops rather than break a rule
days a brief is kept, then deleted

sections.notes: ⛔ NO PRICES ON THIS PAGE. `docs/PRICING_SURFACES.md` counts nine surfaces a charged price has to reach and two of them are edited by hand here; a figure on this page would be a tenth that no guard can see. The band says what the add-on IS and sends the reader to /pricing for what it costs. The middle sentence is the SECOND statement of the A/B gate — card 6 carries the first — and it is worded as the general rule with A/B as its instance, because the add-on is what opens the doors and a door standing on a plan feature still needs that feature. It names no tier, deliberately: `abTesting` is false on free, starter and pro and true from business up in `plan-entitlements.ts`, and a tier name in this band would be a plan table growing on a page that must not carry one. The plan names belong to /pricing, which is generated and reconciled. Unlike the other detail pages the chip is POURED rather than kept: `eyebrow` is set, so the applier writes 'An add-on, not a plan' over the skeleton's 'Now in early access' — the datasets page changed the same chip to 'Included from Starter' by hand, and pouring it is the mechanical version of that. The four stats are figures that do not go stale with the roster: one workspace credit pool with no second meter per feature, the draft-first rule as a number, the two attempts a generation gets before a job stops (`AI_GENERATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS`), and the 180 days a brief is kept. Section background is bg/default (#F8F9FA); the stat figures take the primary.dark token and never the retired brand-blue literal (AGL-1293).

sections.heading: Start from a draft, not a blank canvas.
body: Describe what you want, edit what comes back, and publish it yourself.
sections.notes: Full-bleed gradient band, all text white and centered, the shared 190.72deg literal. Heading is Display/L 56px Black and fits one line at the 900px cap. The body is deliberately short and deliberately ends on 'publish it yourself' — the last thing a reader takes off the page is the draft-first rule, not a feature list.
